name: Hex Dump Decoder
blurb: captured raw bytes split into frames for a chosen protocol
intro: Reads a byte capture in any common hex form (spaced, 0x-prefixed, run-together, hexdump -C or xxd) and splits it into frames: Modbus RTU by CRC, u-blox UBX by header and Fletcher checksum, SLIP (RFC 1055), COBS, or a generic delimiter, fixed length or length-prefixed layout. Each frame is checked and decoded; bytes that fit no frame are reported.

inputs.label: Captured bytes (hex)
inputs.help: Any hex layout; offsets and the ASCII column of hexdump -C / xxd are skipped.

inputs.label: Frame length = field +
inputs.help: Bytes not counted by the length field (header, checksum). AA 55 LEN payload CK: payload length + 4.

examples.title: RS-485 sniff: request, reply, a stray byte, another slave, an exception

usage: Give data as hex text (spaced, 0x-prefixed, run-together, hexdump -C or xxd) and protocol = modbus, ubx, slip, cobs, delim (with delim hex byte), fixed (with fixedLen) or len (with sync hex bytes, lenOff, lenSize 1|2, lenEndian le|be, lenAdjust). Returns one row per frame with offset, length, bytes, check result and a decoded summary, plus counts of valid frames, bad frames and unframed bytes. Use it to make sense of a logic-analyzer or serial capture.
sources: Modbus over Serial Line V1.02 §6.2.2 (CRC-16) and Modbus Application Protocol V1.1b3 §6–7 (function and exception codes)
u-blox 8 / M8 Receiver Description and Protocol Specification, §32.2–32.4 (UBX frame, Fletcher checksum)
RFC 1055, A Nonstandard for Transmission of IP Datagrams over Serial Lines: SLIP
S. Cheshire, M. Baker, 'Consistent Overhead Byte Stuffing', IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking, 1999
